newsitem.title: USA: Green groups plan lawsuit over salmon plan in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Green groups plan lawsuit over salmon plan in U.S.

text.p: A coalition of environmental and fishing organizations has told the federal government it will take legal action against a decision not to list coho salmon as endangered in Oregon.

The move comes after the Clinton administration decided last week to allow Oregon to implement a state plan to protect coho rather than put the species on the endangered species list. The fish was listed as threatened in coastal northern California, home of a much smaller population.
The groups fighting the decision by the National Marine Fisheries Service support Oregon's plan but believe it is insufficient to protect the fish.
The coalition of 25 groups said on Wednesday it planned to sue the federal government in 60 days under the Endangered Species Act.
Mark Hubbard, spokesman for the Oregon Natural Resources Council, said the coalition must give the government a chance to "correct its actions" before filing a lawsuit.
He does not expect any changes.
"We do not expect the National Marine Fisheries Service to turn around and protect coho," Hubbard said.

Oregon's coho salmon plan is based on voluntary measures to protect areas where the fish spawn. The plan, which will cost $30 million over two years, is funded by $15 million from the Legislature, $13.6 million from the state's timber industry and $1.4 million from fishing and gravel industries.
